The current tests establish package, installation, and source-retrieval reliability, but do not establish whether the toolkit improves task outcomes over a capable baseline. Add the first runnable benchmark pilot from the accepted evaluation proposal.

## Outcome

A fresh checkout can validate original benchmark cases, run bounded comparable attempts against a frozen baseline project, independently grade the resulting artifacts, and produce an honest report of correctness, failures, resource use, and limitations. The pilot supports baseline, source-matched baseline, and full-toolkit conditions without silently inheriting personal skills, memories, reference libraries, or grading answers.

## Scope

- Twelve original development cases: easy/medium/hard for DDIA, Software Design, and Doc Agent, plus three integrated challenges. Declare difficulty as provisional until calibrated; do not claim book-exclusive solvability.
- A small shared Python project and explicit task contracts. Reference solutions demonstrate feasibility; executable graders accept alternative correct implementations. Include plausible wrong implementations and correct controls.
- A local Python runner and versioned manifests using existing repository conventions. Separate actor inputs from trusted graders/answers. Verify the actual runtime boundary with denied-read/network canaries; fail closed when an advertised isolation capability is unavailable.
- Three comparison conditions, explicit downloaded/reference-complete resource profiles, source/toolkit/task fingerprints, model and reasoning settings, aggregate run accounting where observable, bounded attempts/timeouts, and machine-readable results. Do not silently report missing usage as zero or treat failed/timed-out attempts as successes.
- Read-only oracles run outside the acting workspace. Correctness and scope failures are hard gates; design/document quality that cannot be objectively established remains an explicit review dimension rather than a keyword score.
- Public development fixtures are not a sealed held-out evaluation set. Document how separate private held-out cases and targeted ablations extend the pilot.
- Exercise a small live calibration after deterministic validation. A full 108-attempt study and the broader all-skill task bank are subsequent campaigns, not evidence to fabricate from smoke checks.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] All 12 task contracts, source states, references, controls, and grader checks are reproducible; reference outputs pass and targeted incorrect outputs fail.
- [x] Baseline isolation excludes personal configuration and unavailable references; the full-toolkit arm uses real installed skills/roles when the selected host supports them.
- [x] Grading answers are inaccessible to actor tools, including alternate paths and network access; unsupported enforcement produces a non-success result with a precise reason.
- [x] Results distinguish setup/infrastructure failures, task failures, timeouts, partial/human review, and verified success; paired reports retain all scheduled attempts and separate setup profiles.
- [x] Tests cover runner boundaries, manifests, result accounting, timeout/cleanup, artifact tampering, and grader controls. Existing installation behavior and specialists remain unchanged.
- [x] Fresh-checkout documentation, a pilot specification, and exact validation commands are included; no private book study, credentials, or personal evaluation artifacts are committed.
- [x] Independent review and verification complete, repository gates pass, a ready PR is opened, and the exact reviewed head is merged after required checks pass.

## Non-goals

No new hosted evaluation service, dashboard, production database, dependency migration, automatic publication of personal book libraries, or claim of toolkit superiority from the calibration. The first pilot is an engineering-core benchmark; recruiter-followup and book-to-agent need their own task families before making all-skill value claims.

## Completion evidence

Merged in #3 as `9d89ddc21b3955cf71320f81dfaa99c8d3d39ed8`. The merged tree matches the reviewed PR head. A clean source archive of `main` passed 146 tests, all twelve reference/wrong-control pairs plus the design sequel, and package validation. CI passed Python 3.11 and 3.13. Independent review and native macOS isolation checks passed.

The bounded one-case live calibration tied on correctness across baseline, source-matched, and toolkit conditions; timeouts and budget-stop diagnostics were retained. A post-rename live check exercised `software_design_agent`, its canonical skill, and the original book section. These results validate the pilot machinery, not toolkit superiority. The full 108-attempt study and broader task bank remain separate work.
